text:
incident-bot: ALERT: increased 5xx rate in eu-west during rolling blue/green deploy for service 'nucleus'. Threshold: >2% sustained for 5m. Paging oncall.
Alex: ack, I'm oncall. Looking at metrics now. :eyes:
Jordan: I'm watching tracing, seeing a spike in 502s from edge -> origin mismatch around 10:12 UTC.
Alex: rolling deploy was at 10:05, blue->green cutover. Which config changed? Ryan? 
Ryan: we flipped feature flag `use-new-router` in eu-west as part of the rollout. Also a DNS weight adjustment was pushed: `eu-west-weights: green=65, blue=35`.
Alex: can we confirm DNS TTLs? Partial resolver caches could still point to blue which doesn't have the new header handling.
Jordan: yes, traces show two request paths: ~65% hitting green (new router) with success, ~35% hitting blue with 502s. Blue pods are returning `503 upstream read error` to edge.
Ana: customer-ops Lina just flagged a support ticket with degraded API calls from an EU customer cluster.
Lina: ticket says ~30% of their requests got 5xx for ~7 minutes. They're asking for root cause and ETA.
Alex: immediate mitigation options: 1) full rollback (flip weights back to blue=100), 2) orchestrated kill-switch for the flag to revert behavior on green, 3) fix blue origin. Which is fastest?
Jordan: rollback of weights is fastest to stop customer impact. But DNS propagation might still keep subset to failing blue if resolvers cached green earlier. However switching weights to blue=100 will push more traffic to prechange code (blue) that is failing, so not ideal.
Ryan: we can disable the new router on green by toggling `use-new-router=false` for green hosts via feature flag backend. That should normalize behavior across both pools if blue and green share identical router code path then.
Alex: do we have a kill-switch command? 
Ryan: yes: `ffctl set nucleus.use-new-router false --env eu-west --sync` (will push to feature flag service and should take effect in ~30s).
Alex: do it. Jordan, monitor 5xx, Lina, update customer.
Ryan: running: ```
$ ffctl set nucleus.use-new-router false --env eu-west --sync
Setting flag nucleus.use-new-router=false for eu-west
Propagation: triggered
``` 
deploy-bot: deploy-hook: feature-flag update queued to rollout service (trace: 0f3a4c)
Jordan: seeing flag change at 10:18 UTC in green pods, metrics show 5xx dropping from 2.8% -> 0.4% within 45s. Good.
Lina: updating customer: "We rolled back a router flag in eu-west; engineers report error rate dropping. Will follow up with postmortem." :white_check_mark:
Alex: incident-bot, please record incident severity and start a call if needed.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: sev: high (customer-impacting, multi-region potential). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/bluegreen-dns-flip. Paging escalation in 5m if unresolved.
Ana: we still need to investigate root cause: why blue started returning 503s during rollout. Hypothesis: config drift in blue origin upstream (proxy timeout), or new routing header compatibility.
Jordan: logs show `upstream read timeout` in blue app logs correlated with a config change on host pool earlier today (nginx keepalive settings). I can open a diff.
Ryan: also, DNS weight shift may have changed request fanout to a subset of origin backends that were recently scaled down for maintenance — they had a stale connection pool.
Alex: action items: Jordan to collect logs and link to incident, Ryan to validate config parity between blue/green origin pools, Ana to coordinate customer comms and severity, Lina to consolidate support tickets. I'll run a controlled canary next time with lower weight and longer warmup.
Jordan: creating log bundle: https://logs.redwood.internal/2791234567/bundle (uploaded)
Ryan: verified config drift: nginx keepalive was 2s on 3 blue nodes, 60s on rest. Suspect TCP churn causing upstream errors when weight changed. I'll patch the three nodes to 60s and restart proxy gracefully.
Alex: timeline update to customer: "We discovered an upstream connection configuration drift in a subset of blue origin nodes that led to elevated 5xx when traffic shifted. We disabled the new router flag to mitigate; we are patching origin nodes and will resume rollout after validation."
Lina: customer ack'd and asked for ETA. We estimate node patching + validation ~25m.
incident-bot: NOTE: Handoff scheduled. Next oncall is Jordan in 40m. If resolved, close incident and attach postmortem.
Alex: leaving a handoff note: current state: 5xxs have dropped to baseline after kill-switch; patching in progress on blue nodes; customer notified; monitoring for 15m stabilization. Jordan will take primary if anything regresses.
Jordan: ack, will monitor. If any regression, I will flip weights back to green=100 and re-open.
Ana: post-incident action: add a safety guard to deployment runbook: block weight shifts >20% per minute for first 10 minutes, and automated parity check for nginx/proxy configs between pools.
Alex: thanks team. I'll start the incident doc and add timeline. Lina, please paste customer ticket IDs here when you have them.
Lina: pasted tickets: #4521, #4522. Adding customer quote and severity.
Alex: handing off to Jordan. Oncall: Jordan.
Jordan: taking over. Monitoring window started. :mag:
